current.thesis: One active manuscript at thesis.md. The protected message is a standalone endpoint object; identity/key trust, authentication, decryption, multipart association, reconstruction and acceptance remain endpoint responsibilities.
current.architecture: No server, directory, database, index, fixed address, rendezvous service, coordinator, orchestration service or external resolver is required for message identity, key resolution, decryption, fragment membership, reconstruction or acceptance. Cryptographic peer identity is distinct from a network address, platform account, storage locator or persistent recipient-to-location relationship. External routes are untrusted, replaceable means of conveying bytes.
current.multipart: Whole-object representation remains baseline. Sender-selectable segmentation is optional and independent of carrier/transport. Any required authenticated membership and reconstruction context travels within the protected representation; no external manifest host or resolver is required.
current.route_acquisition: Recipient acquisition is a route-specific delivery condition and comparative observer topic, not a message-protocol function. OMR/GOMR, Oblivious Signaling, Remise, APIR, vPIR and capability-addressed storage remain external prior-art comparators only.

External routes convey or withhold bytes; they do not establish message identity, membership or acceptance.
Carrier uniqueness, variable placement, concealment and extra hops do not imply anonymity or security.
